function.mechanism: Copper substitution in chlorophyll derivatives improves green colour stability during processing and storage compared with native chlorophyll.
common_food_categories: Citrus-based dry beverage mixes (US-specific use in 21 CFR 73.125)
Other green-coloured foods where nationally authorised

adi.basis: EFSA 2015 re-evaluation states the previous ADI of 15 mg/kg bw/day (as copper chlorophylls) should be withdrawn due insufficient data.

efsa.key_finding: EFSA could not adequately assess safety of E141(i)/(ii) with available data; unresolved composition/genotoxicity concerns and ADI withdrawal recommendation.

adi.basis: WHO/JECFA lists ADI 0-15 mg/kg bw for chlorophylls, copper complexes (INS 141(i)); related INS 141(ii) entries also list 0-15 mg/kg bw.

concerns.summary: EFSA reported that genotoxicity concerns for unidentified fractions of E141(i)/(ii) could not be ruled out under the available dataset.

EFSA identified uncertainty on composition and noted that maximum-level exposure scenarios exceeded the former ADI in younger groups; copper contribution could challenge upper intake limits in toddlers.

no_concern_confirmed: Recent preclinical GLP work reported high-dose tolerability and no clear acute/subacute toxicity signals in rodents.
A recent phase I human study reported tolerability up to high oral doses in healthy adult males in a therapeutic context.
An in vitro human blood study reported no cyto/genotoxic signal at tested concentrations.

adi_exceedance.notes: EFSA maximum-level scenarios were reported above the previous ADI for multiple age groups (not elderly in that scenario).

risk_assessment.rationale: Despite historical JECFA/FDA permissions, EFSA's latest re-evaluation could not confirm safety and recommended withdrawal of the previous ADI, with unresolved compositional/genotoxicity uncertainty and age-group exposure concerns.
key_factors: EFSA inability to complete safety assessment
Exposure concern in younger populations at maximum-level assumptions
No IARC listing and no major-jurisdiction outright ban identified
Recent positive tolerability studies are mostly therapeutic-context and not a full regulatory dietary re-evaluation
